finderFindings.claim: The test stub gets an `as unknown as RotateTool['dragCtx']` cast that hides the missing required fields `xy0` and `angle1`.
finderFindings.scenario: The stub `{ action: { operations: [], perform: () => undefined } }` has no `xy0` or `angle1`, and those fields are required in the new `RotateDragContext`. The double cast hides that from the type checker. If a later change makes the code under test read `dragCtx.xy0` (for example `vectorUtils.calcAngle(dragCtx.xy0, ...)` in mousemove), the test hits `undefined` at runtime instead of failing to compile. The `// @ts-ignore` on line 309 already suppresses the check, so the cast adds nothing. Build a real `RotateDragContext` instead, with `xy0: new Vec2()`, `angle1: 0` and a real `Action`, so the stub matches the declared type.

finderFindings.claim: New `MergeItems` alias is a third local copy of the same `ReturnType<typeof getItemsToFuse>` alias.
finderFindings.scenario: rotate.ts:42 adds `type MergeItems = ReturnType<typeof getItemsToFuse>;`. The same line already exists, unexported, at select/select.types.ts:17 and chain.ts:39, and fragmentSelection.ts:47 writes the same type inline. The rotate tool now has its own copy as well. If `getItemsToFuse` is changed or the merge-items shape gets a single named type (template.types.ts:71 already exports a separate `MergeItems` with a different, nullable shape), each copy has to be found and updated by hand. Export the alias once, for example from select.types.ts next to the other drag-context types, and import it in rotate.ts.

finderFindings.claim: New `as unknown as RotateTool['dragCtx']` cast hides that the stub is missing required members.
finderFindings.scenario: The stub has only `action` and lacks the required `xy0` and `angle1` fields of `RotateDragContext`. Its `action` is a plain object, not an `Action`. The double cast stops the type checker from seeing either problem, and the `// @ts-ignore` on line 309 stays in place too. If a later change makes `mouseup` read `dragCtx.xy0`, the test still compiles but fails at runtime. Build a valid `RotateDragContext` instead: `{ xy0: new Vec2(), angle1: 0, action: new Action() }`. Then remove the cast, and the `@ts-ignore` if it is no longer needed.

finderFindings.claim: `angle`, `action` and `mergeItems` are three separate optional fields, but they mark one phase and are always set together.
finderFindings.scenario: `mousemove` (lines 240-253) sets all three fields together, and nothing else sets them. Because the type makes each one optional on its own, every reader needs its own fallback: `'angle' in dragCtx` at line 237, `?? new Action()` at line 290, `?? 0` at line 306, and `?? {}` at line 271. The next contributor has to keep these fallbacks consistent by hand. If `mouseup` runs before any `mousemove`, it silently records a 0° monomer rotation instead of skipping it. Use a union instead: `{ xy0; angle1 } | { xy0; angle1; rotation: { angle; action; mergeItems } }`, or one optional `rotation` object. That makes the phase explicit and removes the scattered defaults. Also, `!('angle' in dragCtx)` on line 237 is now redundant, because `dragCtx.angle !== rotateAngleInDegrees` already covers the undefined case.
